title: Apply Focus–Glue–Context Fisheye Transformation — fisheye_fgc
text: coords matrix data frame least two columns representing x y coordinates. cx, cy Numeric. x y coordinates fisheye center (default = 0, 0). r_in Numeric. Radius focus zone (default = 0.34). r_out Numeric. Radius glue zone boundary (default = 0.5). zoom_factor Numeric. Expansion factor applied within focus zone (default = 1.5). squeeze_factor Numeric (0,1]. Compression factor applied within glue zone (smaller values = stronger compression, default = 0.3). method Character. "expand" "outward" (default = "expand"). revolution Numeric. Optional rotation factor applied glue zone. Positive values rotate counter-clockwise, negative values clockwise (default = 0.0).

title: Apply Focus–Glue–Context Fisheye Transformation — fisheye_fgc
text: numeric matrix two columns (x_new, y_new) transformed coordinates. Additional attributes: "zones": character vector classifying point "focus", "glue", "context". "original_radius": numeric vector original radial distances. "new_radius": numeric vector transformed radial distances.

title: Apply Focus–Glue–Context Fisheye Transformation — fisheye_fgc
text: function operates three radial zones around chosen center: Focus zone (r <= r_in): expands distances center using zoom_factor, exceed r_in boundary. Glue zone (r_in < r <= r_out): compresses distances using power-law defined squeeze_factor, remaps smoothly connect focus context zones. Context zone (r > r_out): coordinates remain unchanged. Optionally, points glue zone can rotated (revolution) emphasize continuity.

what: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
title: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
text: sf_fisheye() applies focus–glue–context fisheye vector data: (1) ensures sensible projected working CRS, (2) normalizes coordinates around chosen center, (3) calls fisheye_fgc() warp radii, (4) denormalizes back map units, (5) restores original CRS. Inside focus ring (r_in) features enlarge; across glue ring (r_out) transition smoothly; outside, stay nearly unchanged.

title: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
code: sf_fisheye(   sf_obj,   center = NULL,   center_crs = NULL,   normalized_center = FALSE,   cx = NULL,   cy = NULL,   r_in = 0.34,   r_out = 0.5,   zoom_factor = 1.5,   squeeze_factor = 0.35,   method = "expand",   revolution = 0,   target_crs = NULL,   preserve_aspect = TRUE )

title: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
text: sf_obj sf sfc object. Supports POINT, LINESTRING, POLYGON, MULTIPOLYGON. Empty geometries removed processing. center Flexible center specification (see Center selection): numeric length-2 pair interpreted via center_crs lon/lat heuristic, map units lon/lat; sf/sfc geometry, centroid derived; normalized \([-1,1]\) pair normalized_center = TRUE. center_crs Optional CRS numeric center (e.g., "EPSG:4326"). Ignored center sf/sfc object (CRS used). normalized_center Logical. TRUE, center treated normalized \([-1,1]\) coordinate around bbox midpoint. cx, cy Optional center working CRS map units (legacy path, ignored center provided). r_in, r_out Numeric radii (normalized units) defining focus glue boundaries; must satisfy r_out > r_in. zoom_factor Numeric (> 1 enlarge). Focus magnification passed fisheye_fgc(). squeeze_factor Numeric [0, 1]. Glue-zone compression strength passed fisheye_fgc(). method Character; name understood fisheye_fgc() (default "expand"). revolution Numeric (radians); optional angular twist glue zone, passed fisheye_fgc(). target_crs Optional working CRS (anything accepted sf::st_crs() / sf::st_transform()). NULL, projected CRS auto-selected input lon/lat; otherwise input CRS used. preserve_aspect Logical. TRUE (default), use uniform scaling; FALSE, scale axes independently (may stretch shapes).

title: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
text: object top-level class sf_obj (sf sfc), geometry coordinates warped fisheye original CRS restored.

title: Radial fisheye warp for sf/sfc objects (auto-CRS + flexible centers) — sf_fisheye
text: CRS handling. target_crs NULL input geographic (lon/lat), projected working CRS chosen layer’s centroid: Victoria, AU region (≈ 140–150°E, 40–30°S): EPSG:7855 (GDA2020 / MGA55). Otherwise UTM: EPSG:326## (north) EPSG:327## (south). may override target_crs. original CRS restored return. Center selection. fisheye center can supplied multiple ways: center = c(lon, lat), center_crs = "EPSG:4326" (recommended WGS84) another CRS string/object. center = c(x, y) already working CRS map units (meters). center sf/sfc geometry (POINT/LINE/POLYGON/etc.): centroid combined geometry used, transformed working CRS. center = c(cx, cy) normalized coordinates \([-1,1]\) normalized_center = TRUE (relative bbox midpoint scale used normalization). Legacy cx, cy (map units) still accepted used center supplied. Normalization. Let bbox half-width/height sx, sy. preserve_aspect = TRUE (default), uniform scale s = max(sx, sy) maps \((x, y) \mapsto ((x - cx)/s,\, (y - cy)/s)\), r_in/r_out (e.g., 0.34/0.5) interpreted unit-like space. preserve_aspect = FALSE, X Y independently scaled sx sy. Implementation notes. Geometry coordinates transformed st_transform_custom() safely re-closes polygon rings drops Z/M. radial warp delegated fisheye_fgc() (modified).

title: Apply a custom coordinate transform to an sf/sfc object (POINT/LINESTRING/POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON) — st_transform_custom
code: library(sf)  # A simple coordinate transformer: scale and shift scale_shift <- function(coords, sx = 1, sy = 1, dx = 0, dy = 0) {  X <- coords[, 1] * sx + dx  Y <- coords[, 2] * sy + dy   cbind(X, Y) }  # POINT example pt <- st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = 3857) st_transform_custom(pt, transform_fun = scale_shift,                     args = list(sx = 2, sy = 2, dx = 1000, dy = -500)) #> Geometry set for 1 feature  #> Geometry type: POINT #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: 1000 ymin: -500 xmax: 1000 ymax: -500 #> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator #> POINT (1000 -500)  # LINESTRING example ln <- st_sfc(st_linestring(rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(1, 1))), crs = 3857) st_transform_custom(ln, transform_fun = scale_shift,                     args = list(sx = 10, sy = 10)) #> Geometry set for 1 feature  #> Geometry type: LINESTRING #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 10 ymax: 10 #> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator #> LINESTRING (0 0, 10 0, 10 10)  # POLYGON example (unit square) poly <- st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(c(0,0), c(1,0), c(1,1),                                      c(0,1), c(0,0)))), crs = 3857) st_transform_custom(poly, transform_fun = scale_shift,                     args = list(sx = 2, sy = 0.5, dx = 5)) #> Geometry set for 1 feature  #> Geometry type: POLYGON #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 1 ymax: 1 #> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator #> POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1, 0 0))  # MULTIPOLYGON example (two disjoint squares) mp <- st_sfc(st_multipolygon(list(   list(rbind(c(0,0), c(1,0), c(1,1), c(0,1), c(0,0))),   list(rbind(c(2,2), c(3,2), c(3,3), c(2,3), c(2,2))) )), crs = 3857) st_transform_custom(mp, transform_fun = scale_shift,                     args = list(dx = 100, dy = 100)) #> Geometry set for 1 feature  #> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: 100 ymin: 100 xmax: 103 ymax: 103 #> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator #> MULTIPOLYGON (((100 100, 101 100, 101 101, 100 ...  # In an sf data frame sf_df <- st_sf(id = 1:2, geometry = st_sfc(   st_point(c(10, 10)),   st_linestring(rbind(c(0,0), c(2,0), c(2,2))) ), crs = 3857)  st_transform_custom(sf_df, transform_fun = scale_shift,                     args = list(sx = 3, sy = 3)) #> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 1 field #> Geometry type: GEOMETRY #> Dimension:     XY #> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 30 ymax: 30 #> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator #>   id                   geometry #> 1  1              POINT (30 30) #> 2  2 LINESTRING (0 0, 6 0, 6 6)
